html:
The movement of workers, mostly Mossi, from Upper Volta to the plantations, mines and cities of the coast, which began with French forced labour in the 1920s and has continued for a century.

The French drafted men to build the railway and to work on the farms of Ivory Coast, and many more went freely to the cocoa farms of the Gold Coast to earn cash for taxes. After independence the flow went on, and by the 1990s millions of Burkinabe and their children lived in Ivory Coast, where they grew much of the cocoa. The question of their rights fed the Ivorian civil war. Money they send home supports many families. See also Upper Volta.
sum: The movement of workers, mostly Mossi, from Upper Volta to the plantations, mines and cities of the coast, which began with French forced labour in the 1920s and has continued for a century.
